# Contracts of the usage ledger (data-orchestrator-go)

Two generated files, each pinned by the sha256 beside it (the sha256 of the file with CRLF
normalised to LF). Nothing in them is typed by hand, and a copy is never edited: regenerate it
at its source, copy the file and its pin, and run `scripts/check-usage-contract.sh` (it fails when
a copy and its source differ).

| File | Generated by | Read by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `usage-envelopes.v2.json` | `usage-ledger-rs`: `UPDATE_USAGE_FIXTURE=1 cargo test -p usage-ledger-rs --test envelope_fixture`. A byte-for-byte copy of `services/usage-ledger-rs/tests/fixtures/usage-envelopes.v2.json`. | This module: `internal/cost` verifies every envelope with the real verifier and records it through the real consumer (`usage_v2_test.go`, `durable_test.go`, `integration_test.go`). |
| `forwarder-record-request.golden.json` | This module: `UPDATE_FORWARDER_GOLDEN=1 go test -run TestForwarderRequestMatchesItsGoldenAndPin ./internal/cost/` | cost-core (task CR-T4) vendors a byte-for-byte copy and posts every `body` through its real handler, authorizer and strict decoder. |

## `usage-envelopes.v2.json`

Real signed envelopes: each is built by the usage ledger's builder from a provider answer and signed by the real
event signer of the producer that would emit it (embedding-engine, graph-index, retrieval-engine), with the
public key that verifies it and the fields a consumer must read out of it. The keys are throwaway, made when the
file is generated; the private halves are never written down. The envelopes are signed at `signed_at` and live
two minutes, so the tests read them with the verifier's clock set to that moment (a live read) or ten minutes
later (the state of an event that waited in the durable stream).

## `forwarder-record-request.golden.json`

The exact JSON the forwarder posts to cost-core's `POST /api/v1/cost/record` for four reference rows (an exact
contextual-retrieval row, an estimated embedding row, a rerank row with billed units, and a graph row of a
zero-retention organization). cost-core decodes it strictly: a field it does not name is a 400, which is why
cost-core must accept `feature` and `units` before the forwarder is switched on. The `fields` array is the set
of fields the record endpoint names; the forwarder test fails when the forwarder posts a field outside it.
